title: runtime-evolution-advisor-and-lts-fallback-policy
creator: Asha Kapoor
acceptance_criteria: Draft policy clearly defines five change classes and the mapping to semantic version increments
Compatibility-Advisor CLI prototype outputs a migration plan and consumer-impact score for a proposed change
LTS fallback rules described (canary->gradual->fallback) and auto-fallback hook defined
Rollout gate metrics and thresholds documented and added to the runtime release pipeline
Documentation page published and flagged for Security review before merge
description:
Overview:
This ticket captures the runtime evolution policy and the companion Compatibility-Advisor prototype. The goal is to provide deterministic rules for how runtime changes map to version numbers, how deprecations are signaled to customers, and automated rollout gates plus an automated LTS fallback mechanism. The Compatibility-Advisor is a developer-facing checklist + CLI that generates a migration plan and an impact score for proposed changes.

Why this is different / motivation:
We already have several semver and upgrade playbooks, but engineering teams still make inconsistent decisions about what constitutes a breaking change for the serving runtime (e.g., KV-cache format changes vs. API surface changes vs. on-disk model layout). That variability increases customer breakage risk and complicates Dedicated/Private upgrade automation. The advisor plus a clear channel/fallback policy reduces risk and accelerates safe rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Scope:
- Define a concise "Change Class" taxonomy tailored to model-serving runtime concerns.
- Map Change Classes to semantic version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) and to LTS compatibility guarantees.
- Define deprecation signaling in responses and the developer console (headers, runtime metadata, and dashboard alerts).
- Specify rollout gates and automatic fallback criteria (metrics and thresholds).
- Deliver Compatibility-Advisor CLI prototype that: performs static checks against the change diff, runs selected compatibility tests, and emits a migration plan (user-visible breaking points and recommended mitigations).

Change Classes (unique to runtime):
1) Behavioral Fix (patch-safe): internal bugfixes or performance improvements that do not alter API semantics or on-disk formats.
2) Config Schema Extension (minor-safe): additive config fields or optional flags; defaults preserve prior behavior.
3) Non-invasive Feature (minor-safe): new API endpoints or telemetry that are opt-in and do not change existing response shapes.
4) Backwards-affecting Performance/Resource Change (minor or major depending): changes that alter throughput/latency characteristics requiring different autoscale sizing or batch sizing heuristics; if existing contracts preserved -> minor, else major.
5) Compatibility-layer Change (major): changes that alter request/response shapes, wire protocol, persistent KV or model weight layout, or runtime binary ABI. These require a major version and explicit migration steps.

Deprecation / Signaling:
- Add X-Redwood-Deprecation header to responses for any deprecated endpoint/field with values: "sunset=YYYY-MM-DD, replacement=/v2/foo, guidance=https://...".
- Console will surface per-route deprecation notices and a per-tenant migration checklist.
- Deprecation lifecycle: announce (>=90 days), soft-deprecation (warnings in responses), hard removal earliest (>=180 days) unless security-critical.

Versioning format and metadata:
- Core: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (semantic).
- Add build metadata to capture ABI/format hashes: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH+abi.<hash>. The abi hash will change when on-disk or binary ABI changes, even within a patch, but ABI hash differences signal potential incompatibility; such cases must be accompanied by compatibility mitigations.

Rollout gates (automated):
- Canary Stage (0.5% of traffic for 30 minutes): pass if errors increase <0.1% absolute and token-latency p99 increases <10% relative.
- Gradual Ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24h): at each step require SLOs within tolerance and cost-per-token within expected band.
- Cross-tenant Impact Check: run the compatibility test-suite across a sample of tenant snapshots; failure of any critical test blocks ramp.
- Auto-fallback trigger: if error-rate delta >0.5% sustained for 10m OR p99 latency regression >30% for 5m across multiple regions, initiate automated fallback to the most recent compatible LTS image and create incident ticket.

Compatibility-Advisor CLI (prototype):
- Input: git diff / proposed release tag / changelist.
- Outputs: change class, suggested semver bump, consumer-impact score (0-100), list of affected subsystems, and an auto-generated migration plan with steps and required feature flags.
- Hooks: runs unit/integration compatibility test matrix; collects failing tests and links to failures in the dashboard.
- Example: `rwa advise --pr HEAD --target v2.0` -> emits "Change Class: Compatibility-layer Change (major). Recommend MAJOR bump, enable compatibility-fallback by default for 3 releases, publish deprecation notice with header. Run migration tests: ids 121,122,133."

Migration patterns and mitigations:
- When on-disk layout changes are unavoidable, provide dual-read compatibility for at least two minor releases and a migration job that converts persisted data.
- For API shape changes, provide a compatibility shim that translates old payloads until the deprecation window expires.
- For KV cache layout changes, include an on-start warm-up and a metric `kv_migration_progress` surfaced in Console.

Testing and telemetry:
- Expand the compatibility test harness to include Private/Dedicated snapshots (anonymized).
- Add a CI job that fails PRs if Compatibility-Advisor outputs "major" without an attached migration plan and test failures.
- Track long-tail upgrade issues by adding a "post-upgrade regressions" dashboard that correlates runtime version to user-reported incidents.

Rollback and emergency process:
- Define an automated rollback playbook invoked by the release pipeline when fallback thresholds hit.
- Fallback image tagging convention: `lts-<MAJOR>.<MINOR>-fallback-YYYYMMDD` retained for 30 days.
- Post-fallback actions: create follow-up epic, notify affected customers, and open a retrospective with impacted teams.

Operational concerns and tradeoffs discussed during reviews:
- Tradeoff: stricter ABI hashing improves safety but increases patch churn and may force unnecessary major bumps. Proposal: ABI hash differences alone do not mandate a major bump if a clear compatibility shim plus migration exists; must be accompanied by advisor output and tests.
- Tradeoff: longer deprecation windows reduce customer surprises but delay cleanup. Proposal: standard 180-day window with exception flow for urgent removals.

Next steps / immediate action items:
1) Gather feedback from Platform, Runtime, and Dedicated teams on the five change classes (owner: Miguel).
2) Land a minimal Compatibility-Advisor that performs static diff analysis and emits a score (owner: Asha).
3) Add the canary/auto-fallback steps to release pipeline and add dashboard panels for the gate metrics (owner: ReleaseInfra squad).
4) Security review scheduling (owner: Security) - blocking for release if the change touches TLS/crypto or secrets handling.

Review notes so far:
- 2026-02-20 (Design review): Priya Patel: "Please ensure the deprecation header includes a machine-parseable timestamp and replacement link."
- 2026-02-24 (Runtime): Ethan Zhao: "ABI hash approach OK, but we need a short-circuit for micro patches that only change log formatting."
- 2026-03-08 (Release): Laura Kim: "Suggest adding a consumer-impact floor that forces human review for scores > 40."

Open questions (for stakeholder discussion):
- Agreed consumer-impact scoring rubric (weighting for customer-facing vs internal-only changes).
- Exact duration for dual-read compatibility for on-disk layout changes.
- Whether to make ABI hash part of the canonical version string for release assets (pros: traceability; cons: longer tags).

Related tickets and artifacts are linked above. Please review the proposed taxonomy and the Compatibility-Advisor prototype README in the PR linked. Once we agree on the scoring rules, we will add the CI gate that blocks major-labeled PRs without migration plans.
